title: Dependency gate: unify JWS/JWK handling, FIPS backport, and SBOM-based upgrade policy
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Context: Recent dependency scans flagged several high-risk transitive crypto and SSO libraries used across the runtime and auth adaptor layers. Instead of incremental patching, this ticket consolidates a small but high-impact scope: (1) standardize JWS/JWK verification across services to a single vetted implementation, (2) backport a FIPS-compatible OpenSSL build for regulated customers, and (3) introduce SBOM gating + binary signature checks in CI to prevent unexpected transitive upgrades. Goal: reduce attack surface, remove duplicated JWT code paths, and ensure deterministic, auditable upgrades with minimal runtime regressions.
acceptance_criteria: All service token verification paths (gateway, auth-adaptor, runtime api) use the approved JWS verifier library via an internal shim
FIPS-compatible OpenSSL build is available in internal package registry and can be toggled at deployment for private customers
CI enforces an SBOM gating rule: high-severity crypto transitive changes require explicit approver(s) and generate a release note
Automated integration tests exercise JWK rotation, JWKS caching TTLs, and SAML assertion validation in canary cluster
No >5% tail latency regression on 99th percentile token verification benchmarks compared to baseline
Security review sign-off and SBOM published to compliance bucket
tasks: Audit current JWT/JWK/SAML callsites and catalog implementations, collect owners
Prototype internal jws-shim (thin wrapper) and run in gateway shadow mode for 2 weeks
Create FIPS-openSSL backport packages and publish to internal registry with test matrix (Ubuntu20/22, centos, deb)
Add SBOM generation to build pipelines and implement gating policy (auto-fail + reviewer notification for crypto changes)
Tune JWK cache TTL and implement soft-fallback to max-age respecting origin headers
Instrument metrics: token-verify latency histogram, JWK cache hit-rate, SAML parse failures
Rollout plan: shadow -> canary (10%) -> regional ramp -> global with rollback playbook
progress_updates: 2026-01-12: Kickoff meeting with Security, Runtime, and Platform. Agreed on single-jws-shim approach and CI gating as minimal viable scope.
2026-01-22: Completed inventory of 18 callsites across 7 services; two legacy adapters identified for immediate deprecation.
2026-02-01: Prototype jws-shim implemented (Go) and integrated into gateway in shadow mode. Initial compatibility tests passed except for a corner-case with nested detached signatures.
2026-02-11: Published FIPS backport candidate to internal registry; QA found packaging issue on centos image (fixed 2026-02-14).
2026-02-20: SBOM gating RFC merged. CI now emits SBOMs and blocks pipeline on changes to direct crypto deps until approver sign-off.
2026-02-25: Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-01. Preparing canary dashboards and alerting for token-verify errors and P99 latency
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: JWS shim introduces incompatible signature verification semantics -> Mitigation: extensive compatibility test suite, shadow mode for 2 weeks, opt-out feature flag
Risk: FIPS backport causes subtle crypto API changes -> Mitigation: maintain two build profiles, run full e2e tests and engage security engineering for sign-off
Risk: SBOM gating slows developer velocity -> Mitigation: allow emergency bypass flows with post-approval and include clear reviewer SLAs (24 hours)
Risk: JWK cache TTL too long causing stale keys -> Mitigation: implement short TTL with grace window and serve stale while refresh in background
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2026-01-12: Use a single vetted JWS implementation (jose-native fork) behind an internal shim rather than rewriting verifiers in each service.
Decision 2026-01-22: Deprecate legacy 'xml-saml-lite' parser and replace with canonical SAML verifier (audit trail preserved via adapter) rather than attempt piecemeal patches.
Trade-off: FIPS backport increases maintenance surface but is constrained to a build profile and documented upgrade path; chosen due to regulatory customer demand.
Follow-up: Create a lightweight compatibility guide for downstream teams and a migration checklist prior to global rollout. Owner: Lin Zhao. ETA: 2026-03-05
metrics_and_monitoring: Token verify P50/P95/P99 latency (ms) per service
JWK cache hit rate and refresh duration
SAML assertion parse failures per 1M requests
CI SBOM gate false-positive rate and average approval time
qa_plan: Unit tests for shim surface (signature formats, alg edge cases, detached signatures)
Integration tests simulating key rotation and JOSE header variants
Load test to compare token verification latency at 10k RPS against baseline
Canary observability: synthetic JWT sign/verify probes + real-traffic shadow asserts
rollback_plan: Immediate revert of feature flag at gateway to restore previous verifier
Rollback FIPS deploy by switching node pool image tag to non-FIPS build
Escalation: Paging list includes runtime-oncall and security lead; postmortem required within 72 hours if rollback triggered
